he.t: אחר שכתב לך ישובי עשו ותולדותיו בדרך קצרה, שלא היו ספונים וחשובים לפרש היאך נתישבו, וסדר מלחמותיהם איך הורישו את החורי, פירש לך ישובי יעקב ותולדותיו בדרך ארוכה, כל גלגולי סבתם, לפי שהם חשובים לפני המקום להאריך בהם, וכן אתה מוצא בעשרה דורות שמאדם ועד נח, פלוני הוליד פלוני, וכשבא לנח האריך בו, וכן בעשרה דורות שמנח ועד אברהם קצר בהם, ומשהגיע אצל אברהם האריך בו. משל למרגלית שנפלה בין החול, אדם ממשמש בחול וכוברו בכברה עד שמוצא את המרגלית, ומשמצאה, הוא משליך את הצרורות מידו ונוטל המרגלית. (דבר אחר וישב יעקב, הפשתני הזה, נכנסו גמליו טעונים פשתן, הפחמי תמה, אנה יכנס כל הפשתן הזה, היה פיקח אחד משיב לו, ניצוץ אחד יוצא ממפוח שלך ששורף את כולו, כך יעקב, ראה כל האלופים הכתובים למעלה, תמה ואמר, מי יכול לכבוש את כולן, מה כתיב למטה, אלה תולדות יעקב יוסף, וכתיב וְהָיָה בֵּית יַעֲקֹב אֵשׁ וּבֵית יוֹסֵף לֶהָבָה וּבֵית עֵשָו לְקַש, ניצוץ יוצא מיוסף שמכלה ושורף את כולם. ברש"י ישן):

en.t: Yaakov settled, etc.

After it [Scripture] has written for you concerning the settlements of Eisov and his descendants in a concise manner— because they were neither notable nor important enough to warrant a detailed explanation of how they settled, or the narrative of their wars by which they drove out the Chorites; it now proceeds to detail for you the settlements of Yaakov and his descendants at length and the sequence of events which were their cause. Because they are esteemed before God, they deserve to be discussed at length. You also find [this, concerning] the ten generations from Adam to Noach: “So-and-so gave birth to so-and-so.” But, when it came to Noach [Scripture] discussed him at length. Similarly, concerning the ten generations from Noach till Avraham [Scripture] speaks of them in concise terms, and when [the narrative] reaches Avraham it discusses him at length. This is comparable to a jewel that has fallen into the sand. A person searches the sand and sifts it through a sieve until he finds the jewel. Once he finds the jewel, he discards the pebbles from his hand and takes hold of the jewel. (Another explanation of “Yaakov settled:” [There was once] a particular flax dealer whose camels arrived laden with flax. The blacksmith wondered: “Where will all this flax be stored?” There was a wise man there who responded: “Just one spark that goes out from your bellows burns all of it.” Likewise, Yaakov saw all the chiefs [of Eisov] that are enumerated above. he wondered and said: “Who is it that could vanquish them all?” What is written later? “This the history of Yaakov, Yoseif.” For it is written: “The House of Yaakov shall be a fire and the House of Yoseif a flame and the House of Eisov straw.” [I.e.,] a spark will go out from Yoseif and consume them all. From an old edition of Rashi.)

he.t: ואלה של תולדות יעקב, אלה ישוביהם וגלגוליהם, עד שבאו לכלל יישוב. סבה ראשונה, יוסף בן שבע עשרה וגו', על ידי זה נתגלגלו וירדו למצרים, זהו אחר ישוב פשוטו של מקרא, להיות דבר דבור על אופניו. ומדרש אגדה דורש, תלה הכתוב תולדות יעקב ביוסף, מפני כמה דברים, אחת, שכל עצמו של יעקב לא עבד אצל לבן אלא ברחל, ושהיה זיו איקונין של יוסף דומה לו, וכל מה שאירע ליעקב אירע ליוסף, זה נשטם וזה נשטם, זה אחיו מבקש להרגו וזה אחיו מבקשים להרגו, וכן הרבה בבראשית רבה (פד, ו). ועוד נדרש בו, וישב, ביקש יעקב לישב בשלוה, קפץ עליו רוגזו של יוסף, צדיקים מבקשים לישב בשלוה, אומר הקב"ה, לא דיין לצדיקים מה שמתוקן להם לעולם הבא, אלא שמבקשים לישב בשלוה בעולם הזה:

en.t: This is the history of Yaakov.

[Meaning:] This is the history of the children of Yaakov. These are their settlements, and occurrences until they came to their ultimate settlement. The first cause is: “Yoseif at the age of seventeen years.” As a result of this it came about that they went down to Egypt. This follows the plain explanation of Scripture so as to place all phrases in perspective. The Midrash, however, explains [it differently]: Scripture identifies Yaakov’s children as Yoseif for several reasons. First, Yaakov’s entire purpose in working for Lavan was only for the sake of Rochel. [Secondly,] Yoseif’s facial features resembled his [Yaakov’s]. [Also,] everything that happened to Yaakov happened [in similar fashion] to Yoseif: This one was hated, and the other was hated; This one’s brother is seeking to kill him, and the other’s brothers are seeking to kill him. There are many other examples in Bereishis Rabbah. Another Midrashic exposition: “[Yaakov] settled.” Yaakov was seeking to be settled in tranquility, when the troubles of Yoseif were thrust upon him. [Whenever] the righteous seek to be settled in tranquility, God says, “Is it not sufficient for the righteous [to have] what has been prepared for them in the World-to-Come that they should also want to be settled in tranquility in this world?

he.t: שהיה עושה מעשה נערות, מתקן בשערו, ממשמש בעיניו, כדי שיהיה נראה יפה:

en.t: And the lad.
He did things that were childish, he fixed his hair, and touched-up his eyes so that he should appear handsome.

he.t: כלומר, ורגיל אצל בני בלהה, לפי שהיו אחיו מבזין אותן, והוא מקרבן.

en.t: With the sons of Bilhah.
Meaning that he associated with the sons of Bilhah because his brothers would demean them but, he [Yoseif] would be close with them.

he.t: כל רעה שהיה רואה באחיו בני לאה, היה מגיד לאביו, שהיו אוכלין אבר מן החי, ומזלזלין בבני השפחות לקרותן עבדים, וחשודים על העריות. ובשלשתן לקה, על אבר מן החי, וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ שְׂעִיר עִזִּים במכירתו, ולא אכלוהו חי (כדי שילקה בשחיטה) ועל דבה שספר עליהם שקורין לאחיהם עבדים, לְעֶבֶד נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף, ועל העריות שספר עליהם, וַתִּשָּׂא אֵשֶׁת אֲדֹנָיו וגו':

en.t: Bad reports about them.

Any wrong that he would see in his brothers, the sons of Leah, he would relate to his father: that they ate from the limbs of living animals, and that they demeaned the sons of the hand maidens by calling them “slaves,” and that they are suspect in illicit relationships. He [Yoseif] was, in, turn, smitten by these three: 1) “They slaughtered a goat” when he was sold, and they did not eat it while it was alive. 2) For the slander he related about them that they called their brothers “slaves,” Yoseif was sold as a slave. 3) For the illicit relationship that he related about them “His master’s wife cast her [eyes], etc.”

he.t: כל לשון דבה פרלי"ץ בלע"ז. כל מה שהיה יכול לדבר בהם רעה, היה מספר:

en.t: Bad reports
Wherever the term דִבָּה appears it is parladiz in O.F. [gossip]. Whatever bad he could say of them he would relate.

he.t: לשון דּוֹבֵב שִׂפְתֵי יְשֵׁנִים (שיר השירים ז, י):

en.t: Dibah.
Has the same meaning as [דוֹבֵב] in: “He makes speak the lips of the sleeping.”

he.t: שנולד לו לעת זקנתו. ואונקלוס תרגם. בר חכים הוא ליה, כל מה שלמד משם ועבר מסר לו. דבר אחר, שהיה זיו איקונין שלו דומה לו:

en.t: Son of his old age.

1) Because he was born to him in his old age. 2) Onkelos translates it: “He was a wise son to him,” [because] all that he [Yaakov] had learned from Sheim and Eiver, he transmitted to him [Yoseif]. 3) Another explanation: That his [Yoseif’s] facial features were identical to his [Yaakov’s].

he.t: לשון כלי מלת (שבת י:), כמו כַּרְפַּס וּתְכֵלֶת, וכמו כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִים דתמר ואמנון. ומדרש אגדה על שם צרותיו, שנמכר לפוטיפר ולסוחרים ולישמעאלים ולמדינים:

en.t: Colorful.

A term meaning garments of fine wool, as in “Fine linen [כַּרְפַּס], and blue material,” and as the כְּתוֹנֶת הַפַּסִים [that is mentioned] concerning Tamar and Amnon. A Midrashic explanation is [that פַּסִים] is for his [Yoseif’s] misfortunes; that he was sold to Potiphar, traders, Arabs and Midianites.

he.t: מתוך גנותם למדנו שבחם, שלא דברו אחת בפה ואחת בלב:

en.t: They could not speak to him peaceably.
From their denigration we learn their praise, for they did not speak one thing with their mouth [while thinking] another thing in their heart.
Speak to him.
[דַבְּרוֹ is the same as] לְדַבֵּר עִמוֹ —to speak with him.

he.t: כתרגומו מאסרין אסרין, עמרין, וכן נֹשֵׂא אֲלֻמוֹתָיו (תהלים קכו, ו), וכמוהו בלשון משנה והאלומות נוטל ומכריז:

en.t: Binding sheaves.
As Onkelos translates it: binding bundles—sheaves. Similarly: “Carrying its sheaves.” It is similar in Mishnaic Hebrew: “He may take the sheaves and make a pronouncement.”
My sheaf rose.
[קָמָה means] rose up.
And stood up straight.
[Meaning:] to stand steadfastly straight.

he.t: על דבתם רעה שהיה מביא לאביהם:

en.t: And his words.
[Meaning:] for the bad reports about them that he would bring to their father.

he.t: לאחר שספר אותו לאחיו, חזר וספרו לאביו בפניהם:

en.t: He told it to his father and to his brothers.
After he had told it to his brothers he retold it to his father in their presence.
He rebuked him.
Because he was bringing hatred upon himself.

he.t: והלא אמך כבר מתה, והוא לא היה יודע שהדברים מגיעין לבלהה, שגדלתו כאמו (ב"ר פד, יא). ורבותינו למדו מכאן, שאין חלום בלא דברים בטלים, ויעקב נתכוון להוציא הדבר מלב בניו, שלא יקנאוהו, לכך אמר לו הבוא נבוא וגו', כשם שאי אפשר באמך, כך השאר הוא בטל:

en.t: Shall we come?

“Has not your mother already died?” But he [Yaakov] did not know that these things were referring to Bilhah who had raised him [Yoseif] like his mother. However, our Sages learned from here that no dream is without meaningless things. But Yaakov intended [by saying “Shall we come?”] to make his sons ignore the whole matter so that they would not be jealous of him. He, therefore, said to him “Shall we come, etc.” [conveying:] “Just as it is impossible concerning your mother, so is the rest [of the dream] meaningless.”

he.t: היה ממתין ומצפה מתי יבוא, וכן שֹׁמֵר אֱמֻנִים (ישעיה כו, ב), וכן לֹא תִשׁמֹר עַל חַטָּאתִי (איוב יד, טז), לא תמתין:

en.t: Kept the matter in mind.

[I.e.,] he waited and looked forward when it would come to be [fulfilled]. Similarly, “That look forward to the keeping of a promise,” and similarly, “לֹא תִשְׁמוֹר for my sin” [meaning:] do not wait.

he.t: נקוד על את, שלא הלכו אלא לרעות את עצמן (ב"ר פד, יג): (יג)

en.t: To pasture the sheep.
There are dots on the word אֶת [indicating] that they went only to “pasture” themselves.

he.t: לשון ענוה וזריזות, נזדרז למצות אביו, ואף על פי שהיה יודע באחיו ששונאין אותו:

en.t: “Here I am.”
A term indicating humility and readiness. He was ready to fulfill his father’s command, even though he knew that his brothers hated him.

he.t: והלא חברון בהר, שנאמר וַיַּעֲלוּ בַנֶּגֶב וַיָּבֹא עַד חֶבְרוֹן (במדבר יג, כב), אלא מעצה עמוקה של אותו צדיק הקבור בחברון, לקיים מה שנאמר לאברהם בין הבתרים, כִּי גֵר יִהְיֶה זַרְעֲךָ (בראשית טו, יג. סוטה יא):

en.t: From the depths of Chevron.

But, is not Chevron on a mountain, as it is said: “They went up to the South and came until Chevron”? But, [“depth” refers to] the deep wisdom of that righteous man [Avraham] buried in Chevron —to fulfill what was said to Avraham at the Covenant of the Split Pieces “For your descendants will be strangers.”

he.t: מקום מוכן לפורענות, שם קלקלו השבטים, שם ענו את דינה, שם נחלקה מלכות בית דוד, שנאמר וַיֵּלֶךְ רְחַבְעָם שְׁכֶמָה (מלכים־א יב, א):

en.t: And he came to Shechem.

It is a place with a predisposition to misfortunes. There the Tribes sinned. [They sold Yoseif]. There they abused Dinah. There the Kingdom of the House of Dovid was divided, as it is said: “And Rechavom went to Shechem.”

he.t: זה גבריאל (תנחומא וישב ב) שנאמר וְהָאִישׁ גַּבְרִיאֵל (דניאל ט, יא):

en.t: A man found him.
This refers to [the angel] Gavriel, as it is said: “The man [וְהָאִישׁ] Gavriel.”
“They have traveled from here.”
They have removed themselves from [the feeling of] brotherhood.

he.t: לבקש לך נכלי דתות שימיתוך בהם. ולפי פשוטו, שם מקום הוא, ואין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו:

en.t: “Let us go to Doson.”
To seek lawful pretexts concerning you so that they may kill you.” According to the plain meaning it is the name of a place and Scripture never leaves its plain meaning.
They were plotting against him.
They became filled with conspiracies and deviousness.
Against him.
[אוֹתוֹ] is similar to אִתּוֹ —with him [which is the same as] עִמוֹ —with him, meaning אֵלָיו —toward him.

he.t: אמר רבי יצחק מקרא זה אומר דרשני, רוח הקדש אומרת כן, הם אומרים נהרגהו, והכתוב מסיים ונראה מה יהיו חלומותיו, נראה דבר מי יקום, או שלכם או שלי, ואי אפשר שיאמרו הם ונראה מה יהיו חלומותיו, שמכיון שיהרגוהו בטלו חלומותיו:

en.t: “Then we will see what will become of his dreams.”

R. Yitzchok said: This verse says: “Expound upon me.” It is the Divine Spirit that is saying this: They are saying, “Let us kill him,” but, the verse concludes “Let us see what will become of his dreams,” [i.e.,] let us see whose words will be fulfilled, yours or Mine? It is impossible that it was they [the brothers] who said, “Let us see what will become of his dreams,” for once they kill him, his dreams would [automatically] have no meaning.
“Let us not kill him.”
[נֶפֶשׁ should be explained as]: מַכַּת נֶפֶשׁ —a blow to the soul, which refers to killing.

he.t: רוח הקדש העידה על ראובן שלא אמר זאת אלא להציל אותו, שיבא הוא ויטלנו משם, אמר, אני בכור וגדול שבכולן, לא יתלה הסרחון אלא בי:

en.t: To rescue him.

The Divine Spirit testifies concerning Reuvein, that he said this only in order to rescue him, that he may [later] come and rescue him from there. He thought: “I am the firstborn and the oldest of them all; the blame will be put only on me.”
His coat.
[כְּתֹנֶת] is a shirt [or coat].

he.t: הוא שהוסיף לו אביו יותר על אחיו (ב"ר פד, טז):

en.t: The long, colorful coat.
This is an additional one that his father gave him in excess of what was given to the brothers.

he.t: ממשמע שנאמר והבור רק, איני יודע שאין בו מים, מה תלמוד לומר אין בו מים, מים אין בו, אבל נחשים ועקרבים יש בו:

en.t: The pit was empty, there was no water in it.

From the statement: “The pit was empty” don’t I know that there was no water in it? Then what does “There was no water” come to teach? [It teaches] there was no water in it but there were snakes and scorpions in it.

he.t: כתרגומו שיירת, על שם הולכי ארח:

en.t: Caravan.
As Onkelos translates it: “A caravan of” [It is called אֹרְחַת] because they travel the road [אֹרַח].

he.t: למה פרסם הכתוב את משאם, להודיע מתן שכרן של צדיקים, שאין דרכן של ערביים לשאת אלא נפט ועטרן שריחן רע, ולזה נזדמנו בשמים, שלא יוזק מריח רע:

en.t: Their camels were carrying, etc.

Why does Scripture announce what they were carrying? It is to let us know the reward of the righteous. Because it is unusual for Arabs to carry anything, but naphta and itran whose odor is foul. But for this one [Yoseif] it was arranged [that they be carrying] good smelling spices so that he not be harmed by the foul odor.

he.t: כל כנוסי בשמים הרבה קרוי נכאת, וכן וַיַּרְאֵם אֶת כָּל בֵּית נְכֹתֹה (מלכים־ב כ, יג), מרקחת בשמיו. ואונקלוס תרגם לשון שעוה:

en.t: Spices.

Any collection of many types of spices is called נְכֹאת. Similarly, “He showed them the entire house of נְכוֹתֹה .” [נְכֹתֹה meaning:] the place where the spices are mixed. Onkelos, however, translates it was wax.

he.t: שרף הנוטף מעצי הקטף והוא נטף הנמנה עם סמני הקטורת:

en.t: Balsam.
It is a sap that drips from balsam trees. It is [identical with] the נָטָף that is enumerated with the spices of the incense [of the Temple].

he.t: לוטיתא שמו בלשון משנה, ורבותינו פירשו שרש עשב ושמו אשטרולוזיא"ה, במס' נדה (ח.):

en.t: And lotus.
In Mishnaic Hebrew it is called לוֹטִיתָא. Our Sages explained it as an herb root referred to as aristolochia in Maseches Niddah.
What gain?
[מַה בֶּצַע] what profit? as Onkelos translates it.
And cover up his blood.
[Meaning:] and we will conceal his death.

he.t: וקבילו מניה, וכל שמיעה שהיא קבלת דברים, כגון זה, וכגון וַיִּשְׁמַע יַעֲקֹב אֶל אָבִיו, נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע מתורגם נקבל, וכל שהוא שמיעת האוזן, כגון וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת קוֹל ה' אֱלֹהִים מִתְהַלֵּךְ בַּגָּן, וְרִבְקָה שׁוֹמַעַת, וַיִּשְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל, שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶת תְּלוּנֹת, כולן מתורגם ושמעו, ושמעת, ושמע, שמיע קדמי:

en.t: They listened.

[Meaning:] they agreed with him. Everytime the term שְׁמִיעָה is used to mean agreement, as in the case here, and as in “Yaakov listened to his father.” [or] “We will do and we will obey,” Onkelos translates them as נְקַבֵּל. But, wherever it [שְׁמִיעָה] refers to hearing with the ear such as “They heard the voice of God traveling through the garden,” [or] “And Rivkah heard,” [or] “Yisrael heard,” [or] “I heard the complaints,” these are all translated by Onkelos as: they heard, she heard, he heard, it is heard before Me.

he.t: זו היא שיירא אחרת, והודיעך הכתוב, שנמכר פעמים הרבה:

en.t: Midianite merchants passed by.
This was another caravan. This verse indicates that he was sold several times.

he.t: בני יעקב את יוסף מן הבור וימכרוהו לישמעאלים, והישמעאלים למדינים, והמדינים מכרו אותו למצרים:

en.t: They pulled.
Yaakov’s sons [pulled] Yoseif from the pit, and sold him to the Yishmaelites; the Yishmaelites to Midianites, and the Midianites to Egyptians.

he.t: ובמכירתו לא היה שם, שהגיע יומו לילך ולשמש את אביו. דבר אחר, עסוק היה בשקו ובתעניתו על שבלבל יצועי אביו:

en.t: Reuvein returned.

He [Reuvein] was not present when he [Yoseif] was sold, for his day [his turn] had arrived to go and to attend to his father. Another explanation: He was occupied with his sack-cloth and fasting for having disturbed his father’s sleeping arrangement.
Where can I go.
[I.e.,] where can I flee from my father’s grief?
A goat.
Its blood is similar to that of a human.

he.t: זה שמה, וכשהיא דבוקה לתיבה אחרת, כגון כתנת יוסף, כתנת פסים, כתנת בד, נקוד כְּתֹנֶת:

en.t: The coat.

This is [the form of the word as] a noun, [הַכֻּתֹּנֶת]. When it is in the construct state to the word that follows it, for instance, כְּתֹנֶת יוֹסֵף —“Yoseif’s coat.” כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִים —“A colorful coat,” [or] כְּתֹנֶת בַּד —“A linen coat,” it is vocalized thus: כְּתֹנֶת.
And said, “My son’s coat …
is this.”

he.t: נצנצה בו רוח הקדש (ב"ר פד, יט), סופו שתתגרה בו אשת פוטיפר. ולמה לא גלה לו הקב"ה, לפי שהחרימו וקללו את כל מי שיגלה, ושתפו להקב"ה עמהם (תנחומא וישב ב), אבל יצחק היה יודע שהוא חי, אמר, היאך אגלה, והקב"ה אינו רוצה לגלות לו:

en.t: An evil beast has devoured him.

A spark of the Divine Spirit flickered within him. It is his destiny that Potiphar’s wife would provoke him. Why did God not reveal [everything] to him? Because they [the brothers] banned and cursed anyone who would reveal it and they included God with them. Yitzchok, however, knew that he [Yoseif] was alive, but thought: “How can I reveal it when God does not wish to reveal it to him.”

he.t: כ"ב שנה, משפירש ממנו עד שירד יעקב למצרים, שנאמר יוסף בן שבע עשרה שנה וגו', ובן שלשים שנה היה בעמדו לפני פרעה, ושבע שני השובע ושנתים הרעב כשבא יעקב למצרים, הרי כ"ב שנה, כנגד כ"ב שנה שלא קיים יעקב כבוד אב ואם, כ' שנה שהיה בבית לבן, וב' שנה בדרך בשובו מבית לבן, שנה וחצי בסכות וששה חדשים בבית אל (מגילה טז: יז.). וזהו שאמר ללבן זֶה לִי עֶשׂרִים שָׁנָה בְּבֵיתֶךָ, לי הן, עלי הן, וסופי ללקות כנגדן:

en.t: For many days.

Twenty-two years, from when he left him until Yaakov went down to Egypt. As it is said: “Yoseif was seventeen years old, etc.” and he was thirty years old when he stood before Pharoah. [Add] the seven years of plenty and the two years of hunger, at which time Yaakov came to Egypt, which is a total of twenty-two years, corresponding to the twenty-two years that Yaakov did not fulfill the [precept of] honoring one’s father and mother— the twenty years he was at Lavan’s house and the two years he was en route upon his return from Lavan’s house, one and a half years in Sukkos and six months in Beis Eil. This was [the reference] when he said to Lavan, “These twenty years that I have been in your house.” לִי —to me [means] they are upon me—my responsibility and I will ultimately be punished for them.

he.t: רבי יהודה אומר, אחיות תאומות נולדו עם כל שבט ושבט, ונשאום. רבי נחמיה אומר, כנעניות היו, אלא מהו וכל בנותיו, כלותיו, שאין אדם נמנע מלקרוא לחתנו בנו ולכלתו בתו:

en.t: And all his daughters.

R. Yehudah says: A twin sister was born with each brother and each [brother] married one [of the sisters]. R. Nechemia says: [Their wives] were Canaanites. Then what is the meaning of “And all his daughters?” [It means] his daughters-in-law, because a person does not hesitate to call his son-in-law, his son; and his daughter-in-law, his daughter.

he.t: אין אדם מקבל תנחומין על החי (ב"ר פד, כא), וסבור שמת, שעל המת נגזרה גזירה שישתכח מן הלב, ולא על החי:

en.t: But he refused to be consoled.
A person cannot accept consolation for one who is alive, but is thought to be dead, because only for the dead was it decreed that he be forgotten, but not for the living.

he.t: כמו על בני והרבה אל משמשין בלשון על,אֶל שָׁאוּל וְאֶל בֵּית הַדָּמִים (שמואל־ב כא, א), אֶל הִלָּקַח אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים, וְאֶל (מות) חָמִיה וְאִישָׁהּ (שם־א ד, כא):

en.t: “I will go down for my son.”

[אֶל בְּנִי] is the same as עַל בְּנִי — for my son. Many times אֶל [to] is used for עַל [for]. [E.g.,] [אֶל]—“Because of Saul,” [וְאֶל]—“And because of his bloody house,” [or] [אֶל]—“Because the ark of God was taken,” [וְאֶל] “And because of the death of her father-in-law and her husband.”

he.t: כפשוטו לשון קבר הוא, באבלי אקבר ולא אתנחם כל ימי. ומדרשו, גיהנם, סימן זה היה מסור בידי מפי הגבורה, אם לא ימות אחד מבני בחיי, מובטח אני שאיני רואה גיהנם:

en.t: To the grave, mourning.

In its plain sense it [שְׁאֹל] means the grave. [Yaakov’s intent was:] while still mourning will I be buried and not be consoled all of my life. The Midrashic explanation [of שְׁאֹל] is Gehinom [hell]. [I.e.,] this was a sign given to me by God that if none of my children die in my lifetime then I am assured not to see Gehinom.

he.t: יצחק היה בוכה מפני צרתו של יעקב, אבל לא היה מתאבל שהיה יודע שהוא חי:

en.t: His father wept for him.
[“His father” refers to] Yitzchok who cried because of Yaakov’s anguish, but he did not mourn, for he knew that he [Yoseif] was alive.
The slaughterers.
[הַטַבָּחִים means] the slaughterers of the kings animals.

he.t: למה נסמכה פרשה זו לכאן והפסיק בפרשתו של יוסף, ללמד, שהורידוהו אחיו מגדולתו כשראו בצרת אביהם, אמרו, אתה אמרת למכרו, אלו אמרת להשיבו, היינו שומעים לך:

en.t: At that time.

Why is this narrative [of Yehudah] placed here, thereby interrupting the narrative of Yoseif? This is to teach that his brothers demoted him from his important position. When they saw the anguish of their father they said, “You advised us to sell him. Had you advised us to return him we would have listened to you.”
He turned away.
From his brothers.
Until [he came to] a man, an Adullamite.
He had become his business-partner.
A Canaanite.
[Meaning] a merchant.

he.t: שם המקום, ואומר אני, על שם שפסקה מלדת נקרא כזיב, לשון הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לִי כְּמוֹ אַכְזָב, אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְכַזְּבוּ מֵימָיו, דאם לא כן מה בא להודיענו. ובבראשית רבה (פה, ד) ראיתי, ותקרא שמו שלה וגו' פסקת:

en.t: He [Yehudah] was in Keziv.

[Keziv] is the name of the place. It is my opinion that because [there] she ceased giving birth, it was, therefore, named Keziv; from the same term as, “Will you act towards me as a deceiver [אַכְזָב]”? [or] “Whose waters will not cease.” For if this is not [the reason it was called Keziv] why are we informed [of Yehudah’s whereabouts]? In Bereishis Rabbah I saw [the following]: “She named him Sheilah, etc., ceasing.”

he.t: כרעתו של אונן, משחית זרעו, שנאמר באונן וימת גם אותו, כמיתתו של ער מיתתו של אונן. ולמה היה ער משחית זרעו כדי שלא תתעבר ויכחיש יפיה:

en.t: Wicked in the eyes of Adonoy.

The same wickedness as that of Onan. [I.e.] he would waste his seed. For it is said of Onan, God slew him also. [Also, indicating] that Onan’s death was for the same sin as the death of Er. Why did Er waste his seed? So that [his wife] would not conceive thereby diminishing her beauty.
And establish seed.
The son will be called by the name of the one who is dead.

he.t: דש מבפנים וזורה מבחוץ (ב"ר פה, ה):

en.t: He let it go to waste on the ground.
He would thresh [his seed] inside and disperse it on the outside.

he.t: כלומר, דוחה היה אותה בקש, שלא היה בדעתו להשיאה לו:

en.t: He said, etc.
Meaning, he pushed her off with a straw, for he had no intention of having her marry him.

he.t: מוחזקת היא זו שימותו אנשיה (יבמות סד:):

en.t: He said, “Lest he also die like his brothers.”
She is predisposed to her husbands dying.

he.t: ויעל תמנתה לעמוד על גוזזי צאנו:

en.t: And he went up to his sheep shearers.
[This must be interpreted as if it would have said]: “He went up to Timnah to stand by his sheep shearers.”

he.t: ובשמשון הוא אומר וַיֵרֶד שִׁמְשׁוֹן וגו' תִּמְנָתָה (שופטים יד, א), בשפוע ההר היתה יושבת, עולין לה מכאן ויורדין לה מכאן:

en.t: Has come [lit. is going up] to Timnah.

Whereas concerning Shimshon it is said: “Shimshon went down, etc. to Timnah”! [There is no contradiction because] it was situated on the slope of the mountain; from one side they came up to her and from the other side they came down to her.
And disguised herself.
She covered her face so that he not recognize her.

he.t: בפתיחת עינים, בפרשת דרכים שעל דרך תמנתה. ורבותינו דרשו, בפתחו של אברהם אבינו, שכל עינים מצפות לראותו (סוטה י.):

en.t: She sat at the crossroads

[Literally,] at the opening of the eyes, [meaning:] at the crossroads which was on the way to Timnah. Our Sages explain it midrashically. At the entrance [of the tomb] of our father Avraham, whom all eyes longed to see.

he.t: כי ראתה כי גדל שלה וגו'.
לפיכך הפקירה עצמה אצל יהודה, שהיתה מתאוה להעמיד ממנו בנים:

en.t: For she saw that Sheilah had come of age, etc.
That was why she offered herself to Yehudah, for she desired to have children by him.
And thought she was a harlot.
Because she was sitting at the crossroads.

he.t: ולא יכול לראותה ולהכירה. ומדרש רבותינו כי כסתה פניה, כשהיתה בבית חמיה היתה צנועה לפיכך לא חשדה:

en.t: Because she had covered her face.

And he could [therefore] not see nor recognize her. [However,] In the Midrash of our Sages [we find]: Because she [always] covered her face when she was at her father-in-law’s [Yehudah’s] house, she was a modest woman, therefore, he did not suspect her.

he.t: מדרך שהיה בה, נטה אל הדרך אשר היא בה, ובלשון לע"ז דשטורני"ר:

en.t: He turned aside to her on the road.
[Meaning:] from the road which he was [traveling] he turned to the road where she was. In O.F. [וַיֵט means] destolir—to turn.

he.t: הכיני עצמך ודעתך לכך. כל לשון הבה לשון הזמנה הוא, חוץ ממקום שיש לתרגמו בלשון נתינה, ואף אותן של הזמנה קרובים ללשון נתינה הם:

en.t: Please.

[Meaning:] prepare yourself and your mind for this. Wherever the term הָבָה appears it has the meaning of preparation except where it can be translated as giving. Moreover, those that mean preparation can almost be translated as giving.
Security.
[עֵרָבוֹן means] security.

he.t: עזקתך ושושיפך. טבעת שאתה חותם בה, ושמלתך שאתה מתכסה בה:

en.t: Your signet ring, and your wrap.
Onkelos translates it עִזְקָתָךְ וְשׁוֹשִׁיפָךְ [meaning:] the ring that you use as a seal, and the cloak with which you cover yourself.

he.t: גבורים כיוצא בו, צדיקים כיוצא בו:

en.t: And she became pregnant by him.
[She conceived] strong men, as he was; and righteous men, as he was.
The harlot.
[Called קְדֵשָׁה because] she is [מְקוּדֶשֶׁת] totally dedicated and ready for illicit relationships.
“Let her take it.”
[Meaning:] let her keep what she has.

he.t: אם תבקשנה עוד, יתפרסם הדבר ויהיה גנאי, כי מה עלי לעשות עוד לאמת דברי:

en.t: Lest we are humiliated.
If you continue to search for her the thing will become public and will result in disgrace, for what else is there for me to do to be true to my word?

he.t: לפי שרמה יהודה את אביו בגדי עזים, שהטביל כתנת יוסף בדמו, רמוהו גם אותו בגדי עזים (ב"ר פה, ט):

en.t: Behold, I sent her this kid.
Since Yehudah deceived his father with a goat-kid when he dipped Yoseif’s coat in its blood, he, too, was deceived with a goat-kid.

he.t: רובו של ראשון, ורובו של אחרון, ואמצעי שלם (נדה ח:). ולשון כמשלש חדשים, כהשתלש החדשים, כמו וּמִשְׁלֹחַ מָנוֹת (אסתר ט, יט), מִשְׁלוֹחַ יָדָם, וכן תרגום אונקלוס כתלתות ירחיא:

en.t: About three months later.

[Meaning:] most of the first [month] and most of the last [third] and the entire middle [month]. The term כְּמִשְׁלשׁ חֳדָשִׁים means when the months repeated themselves thrice, the same form as וּמִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת —“Sending of portions,” [or] מִשְׁלוֹחַ יָדָם —“Sending forth of their hand.” Onkelos, too, translates it thus. כִּתְלָתוּת יַרְחַיָּא —upon the tripling of the months.

he.t: שם דבר, מעוברת, כמו אִשָּׁה הָרָה, וכמו בָּרָה כַּחַמָּה:

en.t: Her promiscuity has resulted in pregnancy.
An adjective—pregnant, as in אִשָׁה הָרָה —“A pregnant woman,” and as in בָּרָה כַּחַמָה —“Clear as the sun.”

he.t: אמר אפרים מקשאה משום רבי מאיר, בתו של שם היתה שהוא כהן, לפיכך דנוה בשריפה:

en.t: “And let her be burned.”
Ephraim Maksha’ah said in the name of R. Meir: she was the daughter [descendant] of Sheim who was a Kohein. They, therefore, sentenced her to be burned.
She was being taken out.
To be burned.

he.t: לא רצתה להלבין פניו, ולומר ממך אני מעוברת, אלא לאיש אשר אלה לו, אמרה, אם יודה מעצמו, יודה, ואם לאו, ישרפוני ואל אלבין פניו, מכאן אמרו, נוח לו לאדם שיפילוהו לכבשן האש ואל ילבין פני חבירו ברבים:

en.t: And she sent [word] to her father-in-law.

She did not wish to disgrace him by saying, “It is by you that I am pregnant.” But, [instead she said,] “By the man to whom these belong.” She thought: “If he will confess, then let him confess on his own, and if not, then [I prefer to] let them burn me and I will not disgrace him.” From here the Sages concluded: Better for a person to be thrown into a fiery furnace than to publicly disgrace his fellow-man.

he.t: אין נא אלא לשון בקשה, הכר נא בוראך, ואל תאבד שלש נפשות:

en.t: Please recognize.
נָא is used only as a term of pleading, i.e., please recognize [be aware of] your Creator and do not destroy three lives.
She is righteous.
In what she has said.

he.t: היא מעוברת. ורז"ל דרשו, שיצאה בת קול ואמרה, ממני ומאתי יצאו הדברים, לפי שהיתה צנועה בבית חמיה, גזרתי שיצאו ממנה מלכים, ומשבט יהודה גזרתי להעמיד מלכים בישראל:

en.t: [It is] from me—

that she has become pregnant. Our Sages interpreted [מִמֶנִי] midrashically: An ethereal voice said, “From Me [מִמֶנִי] and through Me did these things come to pass. Because she conducted herself modestly in her father-in-law’s house, I have decreed that kings shall descend from her. And it is from the tribe of Yehudah that I have decreed that kings be established for Israel.

he.t: כי בדין עשתה, על אשר לא נתתיה לשלה בני:

en.t: Inasmuch that I did not give her.
[Meaning:] what she did conformed with the law, inasmuch as I did not give her to my son Sheilah.

he.t: יש אומרים לא הוסיף, ויש אומרים לא פסק, (וחבירו גבי אלדד ומידד, וְלֹא יָסָפוּ, ומתרגמינן ולא פסקו):

en.t: He was not … anymore.

Some say [וְלֹא יָסַף means] he did not continue [to be intimate with her]; whereas others say [that it means] he did not cease [being intimate with her]. A similar instance occurs in reference to Eldad and Meidad: “They did not continue [to prophesy],” and Onkelos translates it, “They did not cease.”

he.t: וברבקה הוא אומר וַיִּמְלְאוּ יָמֶיָה לָלֶדֶת, להלן למלאים וכאן לחסרים:

en.t: The time for her to give birth.
But concerning Rivkah it is written: “Her days to give birth were fulfilled!” [This is because] in the latter [the pregnancy] was full term, whereas here they were short [of the full term].

he.t: מלא, ולהלן תומים חסר, לפי שהאחד רשע, אבל אלו שניהם צדיקים:

en.t: There were twins.

It is spelled full [תְּאוֹמִים with an א'] whereas, there it spelled תּוֹמִים, defective [without an א'] because [there] one [Eisov] was evil [defective] but these [Tamar’s twins] were both righteous.

he.t: הוציא האחד ידו לחוץ, ולאחר שקשרה על ידו השני, החזירה:

en.t: One of them put out his hand.
[Meaning:] one extended his hand outside and after she tied the thread on it he withdrew it.
With what strength.
[Meaning:] with what strength you have pushed?

he.t: ארבע ידות כתובות כאן, כנגד ארבע חרמים שמעל עכן שיצא ממנו. ויש אומרים כנגד ארבעה דברים, שלקח אדרת שנער, ושני חתיכות כסף של מאתים שקלים, ולשון זהב (ב"ר פה, יד):

en.t: The one upon whose hand was the scarlet thread.

The word יַד appears here four times, corresponding the four bans violated by Achan, who was descended from him [Zorach]. Others say that it is corresponding to the four things that he took [at the battle of Yericho,] a cloak from Shinar, two chunks of silver worth two hundred shekels, and a strand of gold. From Bereishis Rabbah.
He named him Zorach.
Because of the bright color of the scarlet thread.

he.t: חוזר לענין ראשון, אלא שהפסיק בו כדי לסמוך ירידתו של יהודה למכירתו של יוסף, לומר לך שבשבילו הורידוהו מגדולתו. ועוד, כדי לסמוך מעשה אשתו של פוטיפר למעשה תמר, לומר לך, מה זו לשם שמים אף זו לשם שמים, שראתה באצטרולוגין שלה שעתידה להעמיד בנים ממנו, ואינה יודעת אם ממנה אם מבתה:

en.t: Yoseif was brought down.

[Scripture now] returns to the earlier narrative, but only interrupted it to relate Yehudah’s descent [from power] to the selling of Yoseif, in order to indicate that it was because of him [Yoseif] that they demoted him [Yehudah] from his high position. Also, in order to relate the narrative of Potiphar’s wife to the narrative of Tamar, in order to indicate to you that just as this one [Tamar acted] with pure motives so, too, the other one [Potiphar’s wife] acted with pure motives. She had seen in her astrological signs that she was destined to have children [descended] from him, but she did not know whether it would be from her or whether from her daughter.
That Adonoy was with him.
He would constantly mention the Name of God.
All [that] he possessed.
This is an abbreviated expression, omitting the word אֲשֶׁר —that.
He did not concern himself with anything about him.
[Meaning:] he paid no attention to anything.

he.t: היא אשתו, אלא שדבר בלשון נקייה:

en.t: Except for the bread.
A reference to his wife, but expressed euphemistically.

he.t: כיון שראה עצמו מושל, התחיל אוכל ושותה ומסלסל בשערו,אמר הקב"ה, אביך מתאבל ואתה מסלסל בשערך, אני מגרה בך את הדוב. מיד —

en.t: Yoseif was well-built.
Once he perceived himself as a ruler he began to eat, drink and curl his hair. God said: “Your father is in mourning and you curl your hair! I will provoke the bear against you.” Immediately:
His master’s wife cast her eyes, etc.
Whenever אַחַר is used it means immediately after.
And sin against God.
The descendants of Noach were commanded [to observe] the laws of chastity.
To lie next to her.
Even without intimacy.
To be with her.
In the World-to-Come [in Gehinnom].

he.t: כלומר, ויהי כאשר הגיע יום מיוחד, יום צחוק, יום איד שלהם, שהלכו כולם לבית עבודת אלילים, אמרה, אין לי יום הגון להזקק ליוסף כהיום הזה, אמרה להם, חולה אני ואיני יכולה לילך:

en.t: It was on such a day.

Meaning: it was when a special day arrived— a day of merriment, a day of their idolatrous feasts, when they all went to their temples— that she said, “I have no day as suitable to seduce Yoseif, as this day.” She [therefore] told them, “I am ill and cannot go [to the temple].”

he.t: רב ושמואל, חד אמר מלאכתו ממש, וחד אמר לעשות צרכיו עמה, אלא שנראית לו דמות דיוקנו של אביו וכו', כדאיתא במסכת סוטה (לו:):

en.t: To do his work.

Rav and Shmuel [dispute what this means]: One says, [it means] literally, his work, and the other says he intended to have his way with her, but, his father’s image appeared to him, etc., as is stated in Maseches Sotah.

he.t: הרי זה לשון קצרה, הביא לנו, ולא פירש מי הביאו, ועל בעלה אומרת כן:

en.t: See he brought us.
This is an abbreviated statement. “He brought us,” but it is not made clear who brought him. [Actually,] she was referring to her husband.

he.t: מעבר הנהר, מבני עבר (ב"ר מב, ח), (ס"א מעבר הנהר):

en.t: Hebrew.
One who comes from the other side of the river. [Also,] one who is a descendant of Eiver.
His master.
[The master] of Yoseif.

he.t: לצחק בי, העבד העברי אשר הבאת לנו:

en.t: Came to me.
In order to mock me, [so did] the Hebrew slave that you brought to us.

he.t: בשעת תשמיש אמרה לו כן, וזהו שאמרה, כדברים האלה עשה לי עבדך, עניני תשמיש כאלה:

en.t: When his master heard, etc.
She told him this when they were intimate. This is what she said: “These are the things that your slave did to me.” [I.e.,] intimate things such as these.

he.t: שהיה מקובל לכל רואיו,לשון כלה נאה וחסודה שבמשנה:

en.t: Granting him favor.
So that he was liked by all who saw him, having the same meaning as: “A beautiful bride and well-liked” [that is found] in the Mishnah.
He was the one who did it.
As Onkelos translates it: It was done at his command.
Because Adonoy was with him.
[בַּאֲשֶׁר means] because God was with him.

he.t: לפי שהרגילה אותה ארורה את הצדיק בפי כלם לדבר בו בגנותו, הביא להם הקב"ה סורחנם של אלו, שיפנו אליהם ולא אליו, ועוד שתבוא הרווחה לצדיק על ידיהם:

en.t: After these events.

Because that cursed woman made it a habit that this righteous man be a topic of conversation to all, to speak about him and to demean him, God brought about the offenses of these [people] so that their attention be diverted to these [people] and not to him [Yoseif]. Also, to bring about a respite to the righteous man through their doings.

he.t: זה נמצא זבוב בפיילי פוטירין שלו, וזה נמצא צרור בגלוסקין שלו:

en.t: An offense was committed.
Concerning one, a fly was found in his cup of aromatic beverage while a pebble was found in the bread of the other.

he.t: את פת המלך, ואין לשון אפייה אלא בפת, ובלע"ז פיסטו"ר:

en.t: And baker.
Of the bread of the king. The term אַפִיָה —baking—applies only to bread. In Old French it is pestor [baker].
The chief of the slaughterers appointed Yoseif.
To be with them.
They were under guard for a period of time.
[יָמִים refers to] twelve months.

he.t: ויחלמו שניהם חלום, זהו פשוטו. ומדרשו, כל אחד חלם חלום שניהם, שחלם את חלומו ופתרון חבירו, וזה שנאמר וירא שר האופים כי טוב פתר:

en.t: The two of them had a dream.

Meaning: the same as וַיַחַלְמוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם חֲלוֹם. That is the plain meaning. The Midrashic explanation, however, is: Each of them dreamed the dream of both whereby he dreamed his own dream and the interpretation of the other’s [dream]. That is [what is meant by] what is said: “The chief baker saw that he interpreted well.”

he.t: כל אחד חלם חלום הדומה לפתרון העתיד לבא עליהם:

en.t: Each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
Each of them had a dream that was consistent with the interpretation that was destined to befall them.

he.t: עצבים, כמו סַר וְזָעֵף (מלכים־א כ, ד), זַעַף ה' אֶשָּׂא (מיכה ז, ט):

en.t: Troubled.
[Meaning] sad, as in: “Dejected and sullen,” [or:] “The displeasure of God I will bear.”
Branches.
Long branches that are called wediz in O.F.

he.t: דומה לפורחת והיא כפורחת, נדמה לי בחלומי כאלו היא פורחת, ואחר הפרח עלתה נצה ונעשה סמדר, אשפני"ר בלע"ז, ואחר כך הבשילו, והיא כד אפרחת אפיקת לבלבין, עד כאן תרגום של פורחת. נץ גדול מפרח, כדכתיב וּבֹסֶר גֹמֵל יִהְיֶה נִצָּה (ישעיה יח, ה), וכתיב וַיֹּצֵא פֶרַח, והדר וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ (במדבר יז, כד):

en.t: As if budding.

[Meaning:] It seemed as if it budded, [i.e.,] in my dream it seemed as if it budded. [Meaning:] as if it flowered, and after it budded, the blossoms bloomed and it began to flower, expanin in O.F., after which it produced ripe [grapes]. [As Onkelos translates:] וְהִיא כַד אַפְרַחַת אַפֵּיקַת לַבְלְבִין — “And when it budded, it brought out blossoms” till here is the Targum of the word פּוֹרַחַת. [The budding stage of] נֵץ is larger than that of פֶּרַח. as is written: “The נִצָה will become a ripe grape” and it is written: “It brought forth a blossom” and afterwards: “It brought forth צִיץ [later blossoms].

he.t: כתרגומו ועצרית, והרבה יש בלשון משנה:

en.t: I squeezed.
As Onkelos translates it, “And I pressed.” This word occurs frequently in the Mishnah.

he.t: סימן הם לך לשלשת ימים. ויש מדרשי אגדה הרבה (חולין צב.):

en.t: Are three days.
They are a symbol to you of three days. There are many Midrashic explanations [of these words].

he.t: לשון חשבון, כשיפקוד שאר עבדיו לשרת לפניו בסעודה, ימנה אותך עמהם:

en.t: Pharaoh will lift your head.
יִשָׂא is a term meaning counting— when he will take a count of his other servants to wait on him during the meal, he will count you among them.
Your position.
[Meaning:] your base and your position.

he.t: אשר אם זכרתני אתך, מאחר שייטב לך כפתרוני:

en.t: But remember me.
[כִּי means:] that if you will remember me after things become well for you as I have interpreted.
Please deal kindly with me.
The word נָא is an expression of pleading.

he.t: סלים של נצרים קלופים חורין חורין, ובמקומנו יש הרבה, ודרך מוכרי פת כסנין שקורין אובלי"ש, לתתם באותן סלים:

en.t: Fancy baskets.
Baskets made of peeled willows having many holes. They are prevalent in our country. It is customary for those who sell fancy cakes, that are called obledes [in O.F.], to place them in such baskets.

he.t: יום לידתו, וקורין לו יום גינוסיא. ולשון הולדת, לפי שאין הולד נולד אלא על ידי אחרים, שהחיה מילדת את האשה, ועל כן החיה נקראת מילדת, וכן וּמוֹלְדוֹתַיִךְ בְּיוֹם הוּלֶּדֶת אוֹתָךְ (יחזקאל טז, ד), וכן אַחֲרֵי הֻכַּבֵּס אֶת הַנֶּגַע (ויקרא יג, נה), שכיבוסו על ידי אחרים:

en.t: Pharaoh’s birthday.

[יוֹם הֻלֶּדֶת means] his birthday. It is called Ginusia Day [in Greek]. The הֻלֶּדֶת form [which is הִפְעִיל —passive causative, is used] because the infant is not born unless it is with the aid of others because a midwife helped the woman give birth. It is for this reason that a midwife is called a מְיַלֶּדֶת —one who brings to birth. Similarly, “Your birth—on the day of your birth” or, “After the leprosy is cleansed [הוּכַּבֵּס] away” because it is cleansed by others.

he.t: מנאם עם שאר עבדיו, שהיה מונה המשרתים שישרתו לו בסעודתו, וזכר את אלו בתוכם, כמו שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ, לשון מנין:

en.t: He lifted the head, etc.

[Meaning:] he counted them with his other servants, because he was counting those servants that would wait on him at his feast, he remembered these among them, as in שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ, meaning counting.
The chief butler did not remember.
On that day.

he.t: לאחר מכאן, מפני שתלה בו יוסף לזכרו, הוזקק להיות אסור שתי שנים, שנאמר אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר שָׂם ה' מִבְטַחוֹ וְלֹא פָנָה אֶל רְהָבִים (תהלים מ, ה), ולא בטח על מצרים הקרויים רהב:

en.t: But forgot him.

Afterwards. Because Yoseif depended on him to remember him it necessitated his remaining imprisoned for two years, as is stated: “Fortunate is the man who has made God his trust, and has not turned to the arrogant.” [I.e.,] and does not put his trust in the Egyptians who are called arrogant.
